title: Customer escalation war-room — Acme Payments (prep & action items)
content:
Personal war-room prep notes for Acme Payments outage - draft

Context:
- Incident: Increased 5xx rate and tokenization errors for Acme Payments' invoice-generation flow after model rollout (redwood-model-v2.1.0-quant) beginning 2026-03-02 21:00 UTC.
- Impact: ~30% of invoice-generation requests failing, payment ingestion delayed, 8 enterprise customers affected (Acme primary). Customer reported payment timeouts and duplicate attempts. Severity: P1 for Acme.
- Recent changes: Canary deploy of v2.1.0-quant on Dedicated pool eu-west-1-rt at 2026-03-02 20:45 UTC. Autoscaler policy change 2026-02-28 (lowered scaling threshold for queued requests).

Objective for war-room (short): Stabilize Acme traffic, mitigate user impact, gather RCA signals, agree next steps (rollback vs patch), and align comms.

Pre-meeting checklist (what I need before starting):
- Confirm current error rate and traffic percentage for Acme (Miguel)
- Access to Dedicated pool logs + recent kernel selection traces (SRE dashboard)
- Latest model artifact hash and quantization metadata (Jordan)
- Active rollout config and canary routing weights (Console -> Rollouts)
- Slack channel #acme-incident created and invites sent (Done)

Agenda (30-45m):
1) Quick context + confirm scope (5m)
2) Telemetry recap — metrics we see now (error rate, latency, tokenization errors, CPU/GPU utilization) (5-7m) - Miguel
3) Recent infra & model changes review (5m) - Jordan
4) Short mitigation brainstorm (rollback, scale-up, change routing weights, patch) (8-10m)
5) Decide immediate action + owner assignments (5m)
6) Comms: customer update draft and CS postmortem plan (5m)
7) Follow-ups and deadlines (2-3m)

Key metrics to display in war-room:
- 5xx rate over last 6h and per-customer breakdown
- Tokenization error count and sample payloads
- per-model latency P50/P95/P99 and GPU utilization
- Autoscaler activity (scale events) and queue length
- Recent kernel failures / CUDA OOM traces

Initial hypotheses (brain dump):
- Quantized kernel mismatch with v2.1.0 causing tokenization/runtime mismatch -> tokenization errors
- Autoscaler scale-down too aggressive leading to overloaded instances and 5xx spikes
- Model artifact corrupted during upload to Dedicated pool (partial or mismatched file)

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Immediate rollback to v2.0.9-non-quant on Dedicated (fastest, known-good) — PRO: quick reduction in errors; CON: cost of switching and potential increased latency.
- Increase pool capacity (provision more instances) — PRO: short-term throughput; CON: may not fix tokenization errors if model artifact bad.
- Reduce canary weight to 0% (stop sending new traffic to v2.1.0-quant) — PRO: minimal disruption; CON: existing sessions may still fail.
- Hotfix patch to tokenization code (risky, requires code change and deploy) — PRO: addresses root cause if true.

Immediate proposed action (my recommendation):
1) Reduce canary weight to 0% and route all traffic to previous model (Jordan) — target within 10 min of decision.
2) Snapshot and retain logs/artifacts from affected instances for RCA (SRE/Miguel)
3) Notify Acme with initial acknowledgement and ETA for mitigation (Priya) — update in 15 min and follow-up at T+60m.
4) If rollback reduces errors to baseline within 15-30 min, keep rollback and schedule a rollback postmortem + re-release plan.

Action items (post-meeting format: owner | action | due):
- Jordan | Set canary weight to 0% for redwood-model-v2.1.0-quant in Dedicated eu-west-1-rt and confirm routing | 2026-03-03T15:10Z
- Miguel | Collect error logs, tokenization error samples, kernel traces, and upload to incident folder; confirm error rate baseline | 2026-03-03T15:30Z
- Priya Desai | Draft and send initial customer notification to Acme CSM + ELT (acknowledge, mitigation, ETA) | 2026-03-03T15:15Z
- Jordan | If canary rollback not feasible, coordinate immediate rollback to v2.0.9-non-quant and monitor | 2026-03-03T15:25Z
- SRE Team (assigned: K. Nguyen) | Preserve instance disk images and GPU debug logs for RCA | 2026-03-03T16:00Z
- Asha Patel (me) | Run quick test matrix on staging to validate tokenization behavior between v2.0.9 and v2.1.0-quant | 2026-03-03T16:30Z
- Support Bot | Triage and tag incoming customer messages; route urgent ones to Priya | ongoing

Follow-up notes / comms templates (to copy into Slack/Email):
- Initial customer message (short): "We're investigating elevated errors affecting invoice generation. We've paused the canary for your traffic and are monitoring. We expect a mitigation update in 15 minutes. — Redwood Support"
- Internal status post (Slack #acme-incident): "Action: canary weight -> 0% (Jordan). Monitoring error rate. Miguel collecting logs. Priya on customer comms. ETA for next update: 15m."

Open questions / data needed:
- Are the tokenization errors deterministic for specific payload shapes? (need sample payloads)
- Any recent config changes on Acme side that could affect requests? (CS ask Acme)
- Can we reproduce on staging given the same model artifact and input set? (Asha to run)

Post-meeting plan (RCA cadence):
- T+0-1h: Stabilize traffic, collect logs, customer ack, decide rollback vs patch
- T+1-6h: Deep RCA (artifact verification, kernel logs, reproductions)
- T+24-72h: Postmortem draft + remediation plan (tests, gating rollout, autoscaler threshold tweak)

Notes-to-self (things to remember in meeting):
- Keep comms clear/simple for Acme; they're sensitive to billing/payment impacts.
- Avoid technical blame in first customer message; focus on mitigation and ETA.
- Ask for permission to run sample payloads on staging if needed.

---
End of draft. Will refine during pre-call and share in #acme-incident before join.
